object_description: elongated nine-storey cuboid with two outdoor spaces
design_condition: The building is positioned with its narrow side toward the street to extend the established high-rise pattern and form two differently proportioned outdoor spaces within the plot.

positive.statement: The project develops the established punctiform high-rise pattern into an organizing large-scale form suited to the heterogeneous structural environment.

position.rationale: Elongated high-rise massing is visible; urban-pattern compatibility is anchored on the full volume.

positive.statement: The arrangement of the outdoor space around the building is convincing.

position.rationale: Open-space judgment is anchored to the low perimeter around the elongated building footprint.

positive.statement: The lower-level public-use arrangement creates a convincing functional prelude to the building.

position.rationale: Lower public uses are approximated at the street-facing base of the building.

positive.statement: The educational floors are well structured and provide classrooms of different sizes for contemporary forms of teaching.

position.rationale: Upper repeated floor bands identify the likely educational zone.

positive.statement: The interconnectable classrooms have good and usable room proportions.

position.rationale: Classroom interiors are not distinguishable, so the upper educational envelope provides the anchor.

positive.statement: The façade-open access area provides an outdoor connection and attractive locations for flexibly configurable learning islands.

position.rationale: The access area is constrained to the open street-facing façade edge.

negative.statement: The large forecourt lacks an adequate design and a convincing connection to the first-floor use.

position.rationale: Forecourt is placed at the broad low zone directly in front of the building.

negative.statement: The extra-wide staircase obscures the values and desired moods of the two outdoor spaces.

position.rationale: Stair location is approximated along the front access edge at mid-lower height.

negative.statement: The rear lower-floor room sequences are unattractive and poorly lit.

position.rationale: Rear and lower constraints place the room sequence at the back base of the volume.

negative.statement: The connection between the lower and upper floors appears random and lacks a convincing overall spatial concept.

position.target: connection between lower and upper floors
position.rationale: Vertical connection is approximated through the central stacked building volume.

negative.statement: The administration floors lack vertical connections and zenithal lighting to enrich the closed access corridor.

position.rationale: Administration is assigned to an approximate upper-rear floor region.

negative.statement: The main circulation in the high-rise core is neither functional nor spatially comprehensible.

position.target: main circulation in the high-rise core
position.rationale: Core circulation is anchored centrally within the vertically continuous tower.

negative.statement: The stair system is unrealistic for reaching the upper floors, the number of lifts is too low, and required fire-protection vestibules are absent.

position.target: stair system, lifts, and fire-protection vestibules
position.rationale: Vertical access systems are approximated at the tower core.

negative.statement: The fire-protection glazing, extensive façade, high glass proportion, escape balconies, and external stairs make an economical solution impossible and drive costs upward.

position.target: fire-protection glazing, extensive façade, escape balconies, and external stairs
position.rationale: Extensive vertical façades and external edge elements are visible in the elevations.
